facts.text: A strategy and roadmap must be written to build a new capability for virtual testing of automatic braking safety functions on heavy off-road machines under a hard deadline.
facts.quote: A strategy and roadmap has to be written for building a new technical capability under a hard deadline: virtual testing of a safety function (automatic braking) on heavy off-road machines.

facts.text: The organization planning virtual testing of automatic braking on heavy off-road machines faces high technical uncertainty and has never developed this capability before.
facts.quote: The technical uncertainty is high and the organization has never done this before.

facts.text: About seven months, from October 2026 to April 2027, are available to prepare the virtual-testing capability for automatic braking on heavy off-road machines.
facts.quote: About seven months are available to prepare (October 2026 to April 2027)

facts.text: About four months are available to deliver virtual-testing results for automatic braking on heavy off-road machines after prototype hardware arrives in mid-2027.
facts.quote: followed by about four months to deliver results once prototype hardware arrives in mid-2027.

facts.text: Senior engineers, safety specialists and executives will review the plan for virtual testing of automatic braking on heavy off-road machines, and some reviewers will be skeptical.
facts.quote: Senior engineers, safety specialists and executives will review the plan, and some of them will be skeptical.

facts.text: The planning research was to compare stage gates, technology readiness levels, systems engineering verification and validation planning, test and evaluation master plans, assumption-based planning, discovery-driven planning and other relevant methods, including evidence for each, for high-uncertainty technical programmes with fixed deadlines.
facts.quote: Stage gates, technology readiness levels, systems engineering verification and validation planning, test and evaluation master plans, assumption-based planning, discovery-driven planning and any other relevant method were to be compared, with the evidence for each.

facts.text: Research on credible timeline estimation for new technical work was to cover reference class forecasting, ranges instead of single dates, and known causes of schedule failure in complex programmes.
facts.quote: Reference class forecasting, ranges instead of single dates, and the known causes of schedule failure in complex programmes were to be covered.

facts.text: Research on handling programme risks and unknowns was to cover pre-mortems, risk registers, decision gates, stop criteria and fallback options.
facts.quote: Pre-mortems, risk registers, decision gates, stop criteria and fallback options were to be covered.

facts.text: Research on convincing technical proposals for experts and executives was to cover research funding agencies' question sets, executive communication structures and common reasons proposals are rejected.
facts.quote: The question sets used by research funding agencies, structures for executive communication, and the common reasons proposals are rejected were to be covered.

facts.text: The programme-planning research was required to remain neutral between methods and report evidence both for and against each method.
facts.quote: The research was to stay neutral between methods and report the evidence for and against each one.

facts.text: Each important claim in the programme-planning research was to be labeled as supported by a research study, documented practice of a named organization, or opinion.
facts.quote: Each important claim was to be labeled by its type of evidence (research study, documented practice of a named organization, or opinion)

facts.text: Every source used in the programme-planning research was to be dated.
facts.quote: each source was to be dated.

facts.text: The programme-planning research was to distinguish methods proven to work from methods that are merely popular.
facts.quote: What is proven to work was to be kept separate from what is merely popular.

facts.text: When the programme-planning research found no information, the answer was required to be "not found" rather than a guess.
facts.quote: Where nothing could be found, the answer was to be "not found" rather than a guess.

facts.text: Because the research concerns programme planning rather than machine technology, road-vehicle evidence is flagged only when it concerns technical content, such as virtual-testing credibility frameworks written for automated driving.
facts.quote: evidence from road vehicles is flagged only where it concerns the technical content (for example virtual-testing credibility frameworks written for automated driving).
